questions: What model families preserve instruction-following with long context?
How does KV cache and prefix caching change token cost?
Can tool-calls be executed in private deployment while control plane is hosted?
transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-04-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~54m
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE) — Priya Nair (Head of ML, Citrine), Luca Romano (Platform Eng), Aisha Bello (CTO), Samir Patel (Security)

00:00:03 Jordan Blake: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we, uh, we're Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Maya and Diego. how's everyone doing?
00:00:10 Priya Nair: Good, thanks. excited to dig into this. we are evaluating models and whether we go hosted, dedicated, or private for our customer support agent and knowledge base retrieval.
00:00:22 Maya Chen: Great, Priya. maybe before we start can you give us a quick picture of the workload — throughput, latencies you care about, and what's the context length requirements?
00:00:32 Aisha Bello: Sure. At peak we're looking at about 12 rps overall across channels, with some spikes. important part is long history — we want the agent to see entire case threads, attachments summaries — sometimes that's 50–100k tokens, occasionally more. multilingual support across EN/ES/FR/DE + Portuguese. critical: ability to call internal search and our ticketing tool and prefer minimal PII leaving our environment.
00:01:02 Diego Ruiz: OK so two axes: long context and tool-calling + data residency. Are you currently using any hosted LLMs?
00:01:09 Luca Romano: We've prototyped on a hosted api, but cost and latency are getting out of control when we push long context into the prompt; also not comfortable with some data residency rules.
00:01:20 Jordan Blake: That makes sense. For long context there are a few ways to approach it — larger context models (128k windows and above), retrieval augmented generation with smart prefixing/KV cache, or hybrid: handle long-term history as retrieval chunks and stream in the most relevant spans.
00:01:39 Priya Nair: We tried chunking everything into the prompt but it bloats tokens. curious about Redwood's autosuggested batching and caching features you mentioned in the docs. how aggressive is prefix caching?
00:01:50 Maya Chen: Our runtime supports prefix/KV caching — it will cache commonly seen prefixes and the KV state for transformer layers. For convo-heavy flows the KV cache reduces repeated compute and token sent upstream; in practice we've seen up to 4–6x cost reduction for hot prefixes when combined with retrieval. but it depends on locality of requests.
00:02:12 Samir Patel: is the KV cache stored in our VPC in Private deployment? we can't have caches in third-party networks.
00:02:19 Maya Chen: If you go Private (VPC or on-prem) the runtime, including caches, runs inside your environment. the control plane can be optionally kept in Redwood's hosted control plane, but all inference and cache stay in your network and integrate with your KMS.
00:02:34 Aisha Bello: Good. on the model side — we want to prefer open models for auditability. which families are best for long-form instruction-following and multilingual?
00:02:44 Diego Ruiz: For open models, large mixes exist: Llama2/3 variants, Mistral x family, and some of the newer multilingual-first models. If you need extremely long context out of the box, there are models trained with extended position embeddings or chunked attention — some community variants support up to 1M tokens, but availability and performance vary.
00:03:06 Priya Nair: 1M tokens? that sounds ideal for our case threads, but I assume inference cost and latency will be high. how realistic is that for production?
00:03:15 Maya Chen: It's realistic but tradeoffs: for true 1M windows you need different kernel strategies and memory footprints. our Dedicated pools can be configured with large-memory GPUs and optimized kernels; Dedicated or Private on-prem give predictable throughput and better control over latency. hosted endpoints are possible for extended-context models too, but they may be in higher tier and priced accordingly.
00:03:35 Luca Romano: On quantization — can we quantize these open models and still keep tool-calling and instruction-following fidelity?
00:03:43 Diego Ruiz: Yes, we have quantization profiles. for many workloads 4-bit quantization with fine-tuned kernels preserves instruction behavior. tool-calling (structured output) is mostly unaffected if you avoid aggressive quantization on the final layers for some architectures. Redwood Optimize can recommend profiles per model and per workload.
00:03:59 Priya Nair: How about multilingual performance? We've noticed some Llama variants do OK in Spanish but drop in French legalese. any guidance?
00:04:09 Maya Chen: For multilingual, models trained on diverse corpora or explicitly multilingual families (e.g., certain Mistral multilingual forks, or models labeled as multilingual) perform much better. We often recommend running a small eval suite across your languages to rank models; we can host that benchmark for you inside a sandbox so you can see generation quality and token economics per language.
00:04:29 Aisha Bello: Ok — let's talk tool-calling. We want the assistant to run internal search, fetch attachments, and sometimes execute a ticket update (create or tag). We need safe, auditable tool calls. How does Redwood surface tool invocations?
00:04:45 Maya Chen: Redwood supports function/tool calling patterns — structured outputs that the SE or integration layer can map to actions. In Private deployments tool execution can be done entirely inside your network. You can define allowed endpoints, and we support idempotency tokens, request tracing, and audit logs. We also support a middleware layer for validation and PII scrub before calls.
00:05:05 Samir Patel: Audit logs are important. what retention and export options do you support?
00:05:10 Diego Ruiz: Audit logs are exportable to your S3/GCS endpoints in Private/Dedicated. Hosted has configurable retention tiers. We also support forward hooks to SIEMs and can redact tokens before export if you need.
00:05:22 Priya Nair: One concern — will tool-calling slow down response latency? e.g., calling search then waiting for LLM to re-run with top hits.
00:05:30 Maya Chen: There are patterns to reduce latency: synchronous calls where the model returns a call intent and the orchestrator runs the tool and resumes generation, or async where a staged UI shows interim results. For tight latency SLOs we recommend prefetching, cached search indexes, and using the runtime's streaming API so the end-user gets partial responses while background enrichment happens.
00:05:51 Luca Romano: On security: SSO integration and SAML for Redwood Console? and KMS for key management if we use Private?
00:05:58 Jordan Blake: Yes — SSO/SAML/SCIM for RBAC on the control plane. For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, GCP KMS or HSM). encryption-in-transit and at-rest are standard; we have SOC2 docs I'll share.
00:06:12 Samir Patel: please share the SOC2 and our list of compliance questions — and we'd like an on-prem checklist for air-gapped installs.
00:06:18 Jordan Blake: Will do.
00:06:22 Priya Nair: Pricing — we'd like a ballpark for hosted vs dedicated for 250M tokens/month including embeddings and tool calls.
00:06:29 Jordan Blake: We'll send a pricing/TCO sheet. quick note: cost drivers are model size, context length, and cache hit rate. With caching and retrieval we can typically bring effective per-endpoint cost down compared to naive long prompts. Dedicated also offers lower unit cost at scale.
00:06:46 Aisha Bello: What about vendor lock-in concerns if we use Redwood-specific caching or routing?
00:06:51 Maya Chen: We design with portability in mind. model artifacts are standard ONNX/ggml/flash-attn-fmt when possible, and we provide migration tooling. routing policies and configs are declarative so you can export them. Private on-prem obviously gives you full control.
00:07:05 Priya Nair: For the benchmark — we'd like the Redwood team to run a mixed traffic scenario: multilingual, long history, and tool calls. can you run that in a sandbox with representative latency and cost numbers?
00:07:16 Diego Ruiz: Absolutely — Maya and I can run a benchmark. Priya, could you share sample prompt sets and a small sample of redacted attachments? we'll run with several model variants and return a report with latency percentiles, cost estimates, and quality metrics per language.
00:07:32 Priya Nair: yes we'll prepare that.
00:07:35 Jordan Blake: Great. quick clarification — for the Private option: do you expect to keep control plane hosted or fully on-prem?
00:07:43 Aisha Bello: Ideally keep control plane hosted to avoid maintenance, but we need guarantees that inference and all data caches are fully inside our VPC. also need to ensure key material never leaves our KMS.
00:07:55 Maya Chen: That's a common setup; we support a private control plane too if you want, but a hosted control plane with Private inference nodes in your VPC is a good middle ground and faster time to production.
00:08:07 Samir Patel: Will Redwood support penetration tests or whitebox reviews for Private deployments?
00:08:12 Jordan Blake: Yes, that's part of our enterprise package. We'll coordinate with your security team.
00:08:18 Priya Nair: I have a question about model versioning: we need stable version pinning for canary rollouts and rollback. does Redwood offer per-customer model pinning and gradual rollouts?
00:08:29 Diego Ruiz: Yes — per-route model pinning, canary percentages, and automatic fallback policies. You can also define rollouts by tenant or by route.
00:08:38 Luca Romano: Anything about continuous evals for regression detection?
00:08:42 Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize supports baseline prompt suites and automated quality monitoring; when a model update changes quality we generate alerts and can automatically fallback to a previous pinned model.
00:08:55 Aisha Bello: Good. Are there any sample dashboards we can see for token-level cost breakdowns and latency?
00:09:02 Jordan Blake: We'll include screenshots and access to a demo tenant where you can view per-route dashboards and tracing.
00:09:07 Priya Nair: OK let's talk timeline — we'd like a pilot in the next 6 weeks to validate model and tool integration. is that feasible?
00:09:15 Jordan Blake: Yes. Action items: we'll send pricing and SOC2, Maya/Diego will run benchmarks once you provide prompt sets, and we'll schedule a technical deep-dive to design tool integration and VPC connectivity.
00:09:29 Priya Nair: One last thing — competitor angle: we evaluated some managed vendors but were worried about cost at scale; also considered building our own inference stack but that delays product.
00:09:39 Jordan Blake: Understood. we aim to make the migration path clear and to deliver the bench results so you can compare TCO.
00:09:46 Aisha Bello: Thanks, everyone. good session.

(End of meeting)

Recap (quick):
- Decision points: run benchmark across 3 open-model variants (multilingual + extended context) on Redwood Dedicated and Private; compare hosted as baseline.
- Security: Share SOC2, on-prem checklist, confirm KMS integration patterns.
- Deliverables: pricing/TCO, benchmark report, benchmark window scheduled.
